text:
liv: quick heads-up — seeing a weird perf hysteresis after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday. FP8 paths on Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen are faster for warm sequences but INT8/AWQ suddenly regress on mixed-length traffic. attaching quick notes and a short trace.

sam: ugh, timeline? did this land to prod or just perf-canary?

liv: landed to canary pool at 01:12 UTC (selector v2.3.1). prod rollout paused. main observable: tail latency for INT8 requests jumped ~30% for seq len 64-256, but FP8 still looks good.

diego: do you have perf numbers? microbatch config? batching heuristics changed too?

liv: minimal numbers from perf-run (canary host, 2xA100):
```
model    quant   old_ms/token   new_ms/token   change
mixtral  awq8    5.8            8.1            +39.7%
mixtral  fp8     5.1            5.0            -2.0%
qwen     int8    6.2            8.0            +29.0%
mistral  awq8    6.0            7.9            +31.6%
```
Batches were 64 tokens, batch size 8 (dynamic batching enabled), kv cache warm for ~1k tokens on many tests.

aisha: interesting that fp8 unaffected — suggests kernel path selection favored new fp8 kernels, but int8 kernels are hitting a slower fallback. maybe alignment/packing assumptions changed.

thomas: also check RoPE scale branching. Some of our kernels choose different codegen when rotary dims != head_dim or when heads*kv_dim crosses 8192 boundary. That could flip for some models.

liv: good call. I re-ran with a trimmed workload forcing identical rotary/head dims and saw the regressions vanish. so selector logic must be using a heuristic that mixes head_kv product with seq len to pick kernels.

diego: any KV-cache behavior? evictions or prefetch differences?

liv: yes — on mixed-length traffic we saw higher KV spills to host memory for INT8 path after selector change. memory layout chosen by kernel influences working set size; INT8 kernels with blocked layout increase per-token temp memory, pushing us over eviction threshold. prefetched KV stays in GPU for FP8 kernels.

sam: can you paste the trace snippet where it chooses kernel? the selector logs should show the decision path.

liv: pasted below (abridged):
```
[selector] model=mixtral-11b seq=128 head_kv=64 kv_prod=7040 quant=awq -> kernel=matmul_blk16x64_fused (prefetch=yes)
[selector] model=mixtral-11b seq=512 head_kv=64 kv_prod=7040 quant=fp8 -> kernel=matmul_wave32 (prefetch=yes)
```
Note: blk16x64 path allocs a temp buffer proportional to seq_len*kv_prod/word_per_byte which is fine for small seq, but at mid seq it grows and triggers fallback pages.

aisha: do we have accuracy deltas for AWQ vs GPTQ after calibration? want to ensure not trading too much quality for perf.

liv: short numbers on calibration prompts (calib set of 240 prompts, zero-shot + 5-shot subsets):
- mixtral awq (our AWQ-tuned calibrator): eml delta vs FP16: -0.9% (avg)
- mixtral gptq (our GPTQ pipeline): eml delta vs FP16: -0.6%
- qwen awq: -1.1%
- qwen gptq: -0.7%
So AWQ still slightly worse accuracy but often faster in the old path; now it's slower because of that kernel/layout choice.

thomas: sounds like two axes: correctness/accuracy from quantization, and perf/eviction from kernel memory layout. Fix options:
1) revert selector heuristic to prefer kernels with stable temp memory for INT8/AWQ.
2) update selector cost model to include temp memory footprint and eviction penalty.
3) microbatch ramping change to avoid transient oversized working set.

diego: i'd add a short A/B test: keep selector but pin layout for AWQ->gentle mode where it forces wave kernels until we get better cost model. quick patch possible.

sam: what's impact on throughput if we force wave kernels for AWQ? do we lose FP8 wins on other paths?

liv: forcing wave for AWQ on Mixtral cuts peak throughput by ~6% for short sequences but removes tail latency spike and eliminates GV eviction. overall p90 improves.

aisha: also check calibration prompt distribution. AWQ calibration uses a 50-shot prompt set heavy on long-context completions — that biases kernel choice indirectly because warm kv footprint is different. We should run a mixed-length calibration set (we have prompts/mixlen_calib.json) and re-evaluate.

perf-bot: deploy-checklist triggered: canary cluster flagged regression (ID 6512). tagging oncall.

thomas: plan of action:
- liv: roll back selector commit in canary now and re-run perf-bench for 3h with mixed-length workload (steps: rollback -> restart runtime -> bench script).
- diego: prototype selector cost update to include temp_mem_estimate and eviction_cost. small perf model change.
- aisha: run AWQ/GPTQ accuracy runs using mixlen_calib.json and report deltas.
- sam: coordinate canary hold and prepare communication for SRE if we need forced restart in prod.

liv: started rollback at 02:05 UTC. I'll post a short summary when benches complete.

sam: thanks. and please include a short reproducer command so infra can run it easily.

liv: reproducer example:
```
./bench/run_perf.sh --model mixtral-11b --quant awq --batch 8 --seqs 32,128,512 --duration 180m --calib prompts/mixlen_calib.json --trace selector:info,kernel:debug
```

diego: thanks — will try a variant that forces head_kv parity to see if RoPE scaling boundary effects are the root cause.

liv: ok will share logs in this thread. tagging @thomas for selector cost model review. :eyes:

perf-bot: canary rollback completed at 02:14 UTC. regression flag cleared.

liv: bench run starting now; will update at +30m and +3h.

sam: appreciate it. TL;DR: kernel selector change exposed interplay between quantized kernel memory layout, RoPE/head-kv boundaries, and batching heuristics -> fix in selector cost model and better calibration set needed.
